title: Low-flow rating shift at Hermann
question: Per field measurement below 60,000 ft³/s: does res_log (ln of measured over curve discharge) increase with year?

issues.text: A trend in the residuals shows the rating moved, not why (dredging, upstream dams, datum changes).
issues.fix: Compare the stage at a fixed flow per decade (fit_era) and check the gage's datum history before naming a cause.

issues.text: Measurements are unevenly spread in time (600 a decade in the 1940s-60s, 130 in the 2020s so far).
issues.fix: Also test the decade medians (shift), one value per decade.

alternatives.question: Do flood measurements (≥ 150,000 ft³/s) show the same trend in res_log?
alternatives.why: Drills into the flow class where the floodplain controls; expected flat.

alternatives.question: Has the stage at 40,000 ft³/s fallen at Kansas City and St. Joseph too?
alternatives.why: Expands to the gages upstream, to see whether the degradation is regional.

hypotheses.statement: Low-flow measurements carry more water than the all-years curve says, and more so the later they were made.
hypotheses.null: res_log of low-flow measurements has no trend with year.

hypotheses.statement: Flood measurements show no comparable trend: the channel above the bed sets the stage.
hypotheses.null: res_log of flood measurements rises with year as much as at low flow.

concepts.label: Field measurement
concepts.description: One visit: discharge measured across the section, gage height read.

concepts.label: Stage
concepts.description: Gage height, ft above the gage datum.

concepts.label: Rating residual
concepts.description: ln(measured / curve discharge) against the all-years curve.

strategy.detail: res_log = ln(discharge_cfs / (C (stage_ft − e)^b)) with the all-years fit

concepts.label: Flow class
concepts.why: The bed controls low flows, the channel and floodplain floods.

data.request: Datum changes and gage relocations at USGS 06934500 with their dates
data.source: USGS site description / Water Data time-series metadata
data.why: A datum change shifts all stages at once and would look like a rating shift.

method.summary: A straight line of res_log on year for the low-flow measurements, with a weakly informative prior; the posterior of the slope against 0.

steps.title: Field measurements
steps.detail: Discharge (00060) and gage height (00065) per field_visit_id at USGS-06934500.

steps.title: Fit the all-years curve
steps.detail: Grid over e, least squares of ln Q on ln(h − e) (fit_all).

steps.title: Regress on year
steps.detail: res_log on year, low flows (H1) and floods (H2).

steps.title: Shift or not
steps.detail: Compare the slopes with the per-decade stage at 40,000 ft³/s (fit_era).

caveats: Measurement error is 2-8% or more by rating and is not uniform in time (methods changed from current meters to ADCP).
Measurements cluster in time; residuals within a season are correlated.
Hysteresis: on a rising flood the same stage carries more water than on the falling limb.
A gage datum change would look like a shift; check the site's history.
